newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jinro Group to reduce units to around 10.
newsitem.headline: Jinro Group to reduce units to around 10.

text.p: The troubled Jinro Group would streamline its affiliates to around 10 from the current 24 by mergers or sales, an executive vice president of Jinro Construction Co said on Friday.
Executive Vice President Kim Moon-soo of Jinro Construction said the group would focus on business lines of liquor, trading, construction, engineering, distribution and environmental concerns.
The group would give up its food processing, electric cable and other minor manufacturing operations.
Jinro, the nation's 19th largest conglomerate, or chaebol, announced on Monday it would sell off unprofitable business lines and other assets because of financial pressures.
Jinro held a meeting with possible buyers on Friday to give sales details on real estate, factories and buildings.
About 130 people attended the meeting, including representatives of top chaebol such as Hyundai,
"When we complete our restructuring plan and succeed in selling some of our assets, the number of affiliates will be reduced to around 10," Kim told Reuters. "Or even around seven."
He said the group's equity-to-asset ratio would rise to 25 percent by 1998, when the assets would be sold off, from the current 4.3 percent.
"I'm very positive over the sell-off," Kim said.
The sales would not be done through open tenders, he said. Possible buyers would meet with Jinro executives for further negotiations, he said.
Jinro has asked for 500 billion won in emergency loans from its major creditors Commerical Bank of Korea and SEOULBANK to payback its debts.

Analysts said Jinro's bid to mobilise cash by selling assets would likely fall short as the group would probably have trouble getting the prices it wanted. South Korea has experienced asset deflation on falling real estate prices.
